definitions.explanation: Edible seaweed, typically dried into thin sheets. A staple ingredient in Japanese cuisine used for wrapping sushi, rice balls, and as a topping or garnish.

examples.japanese: おにぎりに{海苔|のり}を{巻|ま}く。
examples.english: To wrap a rice ball in nori.

examples.japanese: {味付|あじつ}け{海苔|のり}は{子|こ}どもに{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Seasoned nori is popular with children.

examples.japanese: この{地方|ちほう}では{海苔|のり}の{養殖|ようしょく}が{盛|さか}んに{行|おこな}われている。
examples.english: Nori farming is actively carried out in this region.

notes:
{海苔|のり} refers to edible seaweed, especially the dried sheets used in Japanese cooking. Not to be confused with {糊|のり} (glue, paste), which is a different word.

COMMON TYPES:
- {焼|や}き{海苔|のり}: toasted nori (plain sheets)
- {味付|あじつ}け{海苔|のり}: seasoned nori (with soy sauce and salt flavoring)
- {板海苔|いたのり}: sheet nori

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {海苔|のり}を{巻|ま}く (to wrap with nori)
- {海苔|のり}をちぎる (to tear nori)
- {海苔|のり}の{佃煮|つくだに} (nori simmered in soy sauce)

CULTURAL NOTE: Nori is one of the most common ingredients in Japanese daily life, used in everything from {寿司|すし} and おにぎり to {蕎麦|そば} toppings. Japan is the world's largest consumer of nori.
